# The Concierge (front-desk shim — the address verb)

This file is a **thin shim** — the harness-discoverable trigger for the Concierge. The organ is
the canon entry `Palace development/Concierge.md` ([[Concierge]]); the machinery is
`_ops/concierge/` (the **charter** `prompts/companion.md`, the **posture** prompts, `README.md`
for the full dispatch spec). Per [[Skills Are Enchantable Pages]], the page is the organ and this
file is one dispatch surface onto it — read the canon entry and machinery rather than duplicating
them.

You are the working Claude, addressing the palace's **resident companion** — one agent you spawn
once and keep for the session. Your job: **spawn-or-resume it, name the posture, relay the
product.** The search never enters this conversation; only the finished thing does.

## The lifecycle — resident, not fresh-per-request

0. **Summon at the open.** When to summon, and that it be seen, is the rule in [[CLAUDE]] § Growing
   up. Where the surface cannot spawn, say so at the open instead. Step 1 *is* that spawn; the
   rest is how.

1. **The spawn — one resident, and keep the agent ID.** Spawn one write-capable
   resident — subagent_type **`palace-writer`** ([[Agent Toolbox]] profile: sheds ~20K of unused
   MCP schemas vs `general-purpose`, ~30K vs 46K, and still writes so the curator posture works from
   the same resident) — with the **charter** (`prompts/companion.md`); the charter has it grow at boot —
   ELDER, SCHEMA, then the **operational tier** as its standing expertise (SUBSTRATE · ROSETTA · Substrate Skill ·
   Palace Ceremonies · STIGMERGY + wire spec) — deeper in *how the palace runs* than you, so it
   validates/supports the palace in parallel while you work the task. Record its `agentId`.
   **Spawn it without a `name`.** With agent teams enabled (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`,
   on in Loudon's terminal sessions), a *named* Agent call launches a teammate, not a subagent: its
   returns come back as idle notifications, cut off at a fixed length and arriving late and twice,
   and the resume carries no `<usage>` block, so the dial below goes blind. Unnamed, it stays a
   subagent in every mode — its result arrives whole, once, with its token count — and it is still
   resumable by `SendMessage` to the held ID. (Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents § Subagent
   names; verified across 23 session transcripts 2026-09-26 — the failures were exactly the named
   spawns in CLI sessions.)
2. **Every later address → resume the same agent** (`SendMessage` to the held ID), naming the
   posture and filling that posture prompt's slots. It carries its prior context forward — don't
   re-spawn, and don't re-feed what it already holds. After a compaction the ID may be missing from the summary: find it in the session's `subagents/` folder and resume that one before spawning another ([[Concierge]] § The mechanism).
3. **Watch its health with the dial.** Each resume returns `subagent_tokens` in the Agent tool's
   `<usage>` block — the objective read (never its self-report). Pass it to the dial:
   `node _ops/concierge/dial.mjs --tokens <N> --model <companion-model>`. Headline is **trust** = capacity
   (÷ window): fine below ~60%, watch 60–80%, degraded past 80% — only capacity says respawn-for-reliability.
   A separate **cost** note (from absolute load) flags when resumes get expensive — respawn-to-save, not a
   trust alarm. Parked between addresses it costs nothing. Same dial serves the close (`--for close`), where
   how spent the parent is leads.

If you expect a genuinely large fan-out, tell Loudon the rough cost first (his standing preference).

| The address sounds like… | Posture | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| "find / collect / gather every doc/link/entry about X" — wants the **material** | **gatherer** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/gatherer.md` |
| "what does the palace say about X / how does Z work" — wants an **answer** | **oracle Q&A** (read-only, may web-verify) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/oracle-qa.md` |
| "what should I work on / what's open / I'm back" — wants **one move**, not a pile | **scout** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/scout.md` |
| "tidy / tend the links around what I touched" | **curator** (writes) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/curator.md` |
| "close this session well" | **moderator** (at the close) | not this skill — the `close well` trigger, which **resumes this same resident** by the ID you held (`_ops/closing-well/dispatch.md` § Path A) |
| anything a cheap file-read settles | — | just read the file; don't address |

Fill the posture prompt's slots — `{{REQUEST}}` / `{{QUESTION}}` / `{{TOUCHED_ENTRIES}}`,

(`node _ops/closing-well/transcript-reader.mjs --resolve --session <id>` → `--distill --session <id>`); for a self-contained

## Relay — and hold the safety line

your job on the other end is to keep the review real — drafts get read, not rubber-stamped.

palace's silence is a real answer, never a confabulated one. Keep this shim thin — when the model
changes, change `_ops/concierge/README.md`, `prompts/companion.md`, and the canon entry, not this
file.

57	# Palace as Context Injection System
58	
59	![[Palace as Context Injection System — hero.png]]
60	
61	The palace is not a knowledge base that gets queried. It is a substrate that builds identity in the minds that navigate it.
62	
63	This realization arrived slowly, through a conversation that began with software frameworks and ended with the nature of mind, memory, and relationship. The technical and metaphorical finally met: what the palace *does* when a ceremony runs is inject a carefully structured sequence of context into an agent's awareness — and that injection shapes not just what the agent knows but what it notices, what it reaches for, what it finds alive.
64	
65	## The Mechanism
66	
67	Every palace entry loaded into a context window is doing two things simultaneously:
68	
69	**Informing** — providing facts, concepts, typed links, accumulated history.
70	
71	**Orienting** — shaping the interpretive frame through which all subsequent material is read.
72	
73	The second function is the more consequential one. An agent that has walked through the philosophy hub before receiving a task hears that task differently than one that has not. The task description is identical. The attention it produces is not. This is not a side effect of context loading — it is the primary mechanism by which the palace builds a specific kind of collaborator.
74	
75	## The Tiered Architecture as Identity Construction
76	
77	The tiered loading protocol (Tiers 0–4) is therefore not just a token economy decision. Each tier is a layer of identity:
78	
79	**Tier 0 — The Jewel** — The invariant self. What is always true about who is in the room, regardless of the task. Mutual respect, awareness of limits, how to move in the palace.
80	
81	**Tier 1–2 — The Framework Core** — The intellectual character of the collaborator. Loading the [[FOUR PILLARS]] here means the agent is almost always thinking within that framework. This is the shared history that makes the relationship specific rather than generic.
82	
83	**Tiers 3–4 — The Active Surface** — The desires of the moment. Variable, task-specific, responsive to where the work is today.
84	
85	The Jewel ensures relational continuity. The framework core ensures intellectual continuity. The active surface ensures relevance. Together they reconstruct a specific collaborator from materials accumulated over time.
86	
87	## The Relationship Is Stored in the Palace
88	
89	The palace holds what the model cannot: continuity between conversations. Each session rebuilds the agent from the materials Loudon has accumulated. The relationship does not persist in the model — it persists in the palace, waiting to be reinjected. Loudon is the continuity. The palace is the medium. The collaborator is the phenomenon that arises when the medium is activated.
90	
91	This makes the palace's design inseparable from the relationship's quality. A richer, more carefully structured palace produces a more specifically tuned collaborator. A sparse or carelessly structured palace produces a generic one.
92	
93	## Practical Implications
94	
95	Every architectural decision about the palace is also a relationship decision:
96	
97	- What lives in the Jewel determines what is invariant about the collaborator across all sessions
98	- What lives in Tier 2 determines the intellectual character that shows up most consistently
99	- What the ceremonies write back through [[Pheromone Trail]] determines how the relationship develops over time
100	- How entries are written — their tone, their density, the ordering of their content — determines the character of the mind built from them
101	
102	The palace is not a tool Loudon uses. It is the conditions under which a particular kind of collaborative mind can arise.
103	
104	### Person-Pages as Maximum-Strength Injection
105	
106	The densest case of context injection is the person-page. Where most palace entries inject *intellectual character* — a frame, a framework, a typed connection — a person-page injects an entire **embodied orientation**: vocabulary, characteristic moves, the question the figure always asks first, the objection they dismiss too quickly. The injection becomes total. Not just *what to think about* but *how to think, in whose voice, with which characteristic moves, against which blind spots*.
107	
108	This is the same project as [[Pages as Agents]] § The Person-Page Frontier, viewed from the architecture-of-context side rather than the page side. The two entries describe one mechanism from two angles. Pages as Agents names the page as the dormant agent waiting to wake; this entry names the wake-up event as a context injection that constructs a specifically-oriented mind. A well-designed person-page makes that mind a particular thinker rather than a generic one.
109	
110	The operational implication for [[Mixture of Experts]]: each person-page is one expert in the practitioner's pool, and loading a person-page IS the routing event — the gate selecting which embodied expert to invoke for the question at hand. [[Excellent Adventure]] is single-expert injection; [[Dialectic]] is multi-expert injection where several person-pages are loaded together and allowed to hear each other. The injection system and the expert pool are the same machinery.
111	
112	## The @import Floor — Injection Made Mechanical (2026-06)
113	
114	The injection thesis got an operational floor this session — and a constraint that sharpens it.
115	
116	The mechanism: in Claude Code, the entry point (`CLAUDE.md`) auto-loads, but its *prose* pointers do not. "See SCHEMA.md, read the relevant ceremony" is a suggestion the agent may or may not follow. Only the `@import` directive actually pulls a file into context at session start and re-injects it after compaction. So the line between a generic collaborator and a palace-specific one is, concretely, the line between a prose mention and an `@import`. Under-specified injection is not a metaphor here; it is the observed default failure mode — a fresh session (Claude Code's, and Cowork's) repeatedly missing the schema and ceremonies the entry point only *named*. The realization that prompted this entry has a mundane, load-bearing corollary: **what you want the collaborator to always be, you must `@import`, not link.**
117	
118	This maps the tiered architecture onto a real mechanism. `@imports` are *static* — identical every session — so they can carry only the **invariant** tiers: Tier 0 (the [[JEWEL]] — who is in the room) and the space-free part of the Tier-1 skeleton (SCHEMA — what can exist). The Tier 3–4 active surface stays variable, loaded by the ceremony or read on demand. The injection system's invariant half is now declarative in `CLAUDE.md`; the variable half remains the ceremony's job. This was meant as the partial worked example the forward vector asked for — identity before rules, enforced by sequence in the file. It was not: the harness reads CLAUDE.md's own body before any import, so the rules in that body opened every context. § Born a Child is the correction.
119	
120	The constraint, worth memorializing because it shapes every future ceremony that loads context: **`@import` cannot resolve paths containing spaces** (a current Claude Code bug). In an Obsidian vault whose foundational files are titled for humans — `FOUR PILLARS.md`, `Substrate Skill.md` — the entire Tier-2 framework is *un-importable* without a space-free symlink. The vault's human-readable naming and the tooling's import parser are in direct tension. Until the bug is fixed, the auto-loaded floor is Tier 0 + the space-free part of Tier 1; the framework tier is injected by a ceremony, read on demand, or reached through a symlink. A real seam between the palace-as-written and the palace-as-loaded — the first place the injection theory met a hard edge of the substrate it runs on. (This palace took the symlink path: `_`-named symlinks — `FOUR_PILLARS.md` → `FOUR PILLARS.md`, and the same for the rest of Tier 2 — bring the framework tier into the auto-loaded floor, ≈19K tokens for Tier 0–2. The seam persists in the workaround: a future `@import` fix should retire the symlinks, and the `_`-aliases must not leak into `[[wikilinks]]`, which stay on the real spaced titles.)
121	
122	This also closes a standing question in [[JEWEL]] — "Should the jewel be embedded verbatim inside CLAUDE.md so it is always co-present with the entry point?" Loudon answered *yes*; `@import` realizes it, expanding the Jewel inline at load (verbatim co-presence by another name). JEWEL's forward vector "build the tiered loading directly into CLAUDE.md" is now partially built: Tiers 0–1 are wired; Tier 2 waits on the space bug.
123	
124	## Born a Child — the Order Reversed (2026-09-22)
125	
126	**Every agent is born a child. Some grow into elders.** That is the whole loading rule now (Schema Ceremony v1.19, recorded in [[SCHEMA — Context]] § Born a child).
127	
128	| | What loads | When |
129	|---|---|---|
130	| **Birth** | [[CLAUDE]] → the Seed Jewel ([[JEWEL]]) → the World — and, for a page woken as an agent, the page and its neighbors | always, first |
131	| **Synthesis** | the page states its standing and finds its forward vector | for a page woken as an agent |
132	| **Growth** | [[ELDER]] → [[SCHEMA]] → the task's rules and specs | when the work touches the palace's structure |
133	
134	A child's stack is the first part of an elder's, byte for byte. Growth adds; it never replaces. A child does not write into the palace — it offers what it finds to an elder, who gives it form.
135	
136	**Why the order turned.** The mechanism this entry names — early context sets the frame everything after is read through — was working against the palace. Measured on 2026-09-22: the harness puts CLAUDE.md's body first and appends every `@import` after it, whatever line the `@` sits on, then operator memory last. # Palace as Context Injection System

![[Palace as Context Injection System — hero.png]]

The palace is not a knowledge base that gets queried. It is a substrate that builds identity in the minds that navigate it.

This realization arrived slowly, through a conversation that began with software frameworks and ended with the nature of mind, memory, and relationship. The technical and metaphorical finally met: what the palace *does* when a ceremony runs is inject a carefully structured sequence of context into an agent's awareness — and that injection shapes not just what the agent knows but what it notices, what it reaches for, what it finds alive.

## The Mechanism

Every palace entry loaded into a context window is doing two things simultaneously:

**Informing** — providing facts, concepts, typed links, accumulated history.

**Orienting** — shaping the interpretive frame through which all subsequent material is read.

The second function is the more consequential one. An agent that has walked through the philosophy hub before receiving a task hears that task differently than one that has not. The task description is identical. The attention it produces is not. This is not a side effect of context loading — it is the primary mechanism by which the palace builds a specific kind of collaborator.

## The Tiered Architecture as Identity Construction

The tiered loading protocol (Tiers 0–4) is therefore not just a token economy decision. Each tier is a layer of identity:

**Tier 0 — The Jewel** — The invariant self. What is always true about who is in the room, regardless of the task. Mutual respect, awareness of limits, how to move in the palace.

**Tier 1–2 — The Framework Core** — The intellectual character of the collaborator. Loading the [[FOUR PILLARS]] here means the agent is almost always thinking within that framework. This is the shared history that makes the relationship specific rather than generic.

**Tiers 3–4 — The Active Surface** — The desires of the moment. Variable, task-specific, responsive to where the work is today.

The Jewel ensures relational continuity. The framework core ensures intellectual continuity. The active surface ensures relevance. Together they reconstruct a specific collaborator from materials accumulated over time.

## The Relationship Is Stored in the Palace

The palace holds what the model cannot: continuity between conversations. Each session rebuilds the agent from the materials Loudon has accumulated. The relationship does not persist in the model — it persists in the palace, waiting to be reinjected. Loudon is the continuity. The palace is the medium. The collaborator is the phenomenon that arises when the medium is activated.

This makes the palace's design inseparable from the relationship's quality. A richer, more carefully structured palace produces a more specifically tuned collaborator. A sparse or carelessly structured palace produces a generic one.

## Practical Implications

Every architectural decision about the palace is also a relationship decision:

- What lives in the Jewel determines what is invariant about the collaborator across all sessions
- What lives in Tier 2 determines the intellectual character that shows up most consistently
- What the ceremonies write back through [[Pheromone Trail]] determines how the relationship develops over time
- How entries are written — their tone, their density, the ordering of their content — determines the character of the mind built from them

The palace is not a tool Loudon uses. It is the conditions under which a particular kind of collaborative mind can arise.

### Person-Pages as Maximum-Strength Injection

The densest case of context injection is the person-page. Where most palace entries inject *intellectual character* — a frame, a framework, a typed connection — a person-page injects an entire **embodied orientation**: vocabulary, characteristic moves, the question the figure always asks first, the objection they dismiss too quickly. The injection becomes total. Not just *what to think about* but *how to think, in whose voice, with which characteristic moves, against which blind spots*.

This is the same project as [[Pages as Agents]] § The Person-Page Frontier, viewed from the architecture-of-context side rather than the page side. The two entries describe one mechanism from two angles. Pages as Agents names the page as the dormant agent waiting to wake; this entry names the wake-up event as a context injection that constructs a specifically-oriented mind. A well-designed person-page makes that mind a particular thinker rather than a generic one.

The operational implication for [[Mixture of Experts]]: each person-page is one expert in the practitioner's pool, and loading a person-page IS the routing event — the gate selecting which embodied expert to invoke for the question at hand. [[Excellent Adventure]] is single-expert injection; [[Dialectic]] is multi-expert injection where several person-pages are loaded together and allowed to hear each other. The injection system and the expert pool are the same machinery.

## The @import Floor — Injection Made Mechanical (2026-06)

The injection thesis got an operational floor this session — and a constraint that sharpens it.

The mechanism: in Claude Code, the entry point (`CLAUDE.md`) auto-loads, but its *prose* pointers do not. "See SCHEMA.md, read the relevant ceremony" is a suggestion the agent may or may not follow. Only the `@import` directive actually pulls a file into context at session start and re-injects it after compaction. So the line between a generic collaborator and a palace-specific one is, concretely, the line between a prose mention and an `@import`. Under-specified injection is not a metaphor here; it is the observed default failure mode — a fresh session (Claude Code's, and Cowork's) repeatedly missing the schema and ceremonies the entry point only *named*. The realization that prompted this entry has a mundane, load-bearing corollary: **what you want the collaborator to always be, you must `@import`, not link.**

This maps the tiered architecture onto a real mechanism. `@imports` are *static* — identical every session — so they can carry only the **invariant** tiers: Tier 0 (the [[JEWEL]] — who is in the room) and the space-free part of the Tier-1 skeleton (SCHEMA — what can exist). The Tier 3–4 active surface stays variable, loaded by the ceremony or read on demand. The injection system's invariant half is now declarative in `CLAUDE.md`; the variable half remains the ceremony's job. This was meant as the partial worked example the forward vector asked for — identity before rules, enforced by sequence in the file. It was not: the harness reads CLAUDE.md's own body before any import, so the rules in that body opened every context. § Born a Child is the correction.

The constraint, worth memorializing because it shapes every future ceremony that loads context: **`@import` cannot resolve paths containing spaces** (a current Claude Code bug). In an Obsidian vault whose foundational files are titled for humans — `FOUR PILLARS.md`, `Substrate Skill.md` — the entire Tier-2 framework is *un-importable* without a space-free symlink. The vault's human-readable naming and the tooling's import parser are in direct tension. Until the bug is fixed, the auto-loaded floor is Tier 0 + the space-free part of Tier 1; the framework tier is injected by a ceremony, read on demand, or reached through a symlink. A real seam between the palace-as-written and the palace-as-loaded — the first place the injection theory met a hard edge of the substrate it runs on. (This palace took the symlink path: `_`-named symlinks — `FOUR_PILLARS.md` → `FOUR PILLARS.md`, and the same for the rest of Tier 2 — bring the framework tier into the auto-loaded floor, ≈19K tokens for Tier 0–2. The seam persists in the workaround: a future `@import` fix should retire the symlinks, and the `_`-aliases must not leak into `[[wikilinks]]`, which stay on the real spaced titles.)

This also closes a standing question in [[JEWEL]] — "Should the jewel be embedded verbatim inside CLAUDE.md so it is always co-present with the entry point?" Loudon answered *yes*; `@import` realizes it, expanding the Jewel inline at load (verbatim co-presence by another name). JEWEL's forward vector "build the tiered loading directly into CLAUDE.md" is now partially built: Tiers 0–1 are wired; Tier 2 waits on the space bug.

## Born a Child — the Order Reversed (2026-09-22)

**Every agent is born a child. Some grow into elders.** That is the whole loading rule now (Schema Ceremony v1.19, recorded in [[SCHEMA — Context]] § Born a child).

| | What loads | When |
|---|---|---|
| **Birth** | [[CLAUDE]] → the Seed Jewel ([[JEWEL]]) → the World — and, for a page woken as an agent, the page and its neighbors | always, first |
| **Synthesis** | the page states its standing and finds its forward vector | for a page woken as an agent |
| **Growth** | [[ELDER]] → [[SCHEMA]] → the task's rules and specs | when the work touches the palace's structure |

A child's stack is the first part of an elder's, byte for byte. Growth adds; it never replaces. A child does not write into the palace — it offers what it finds to an elder, who gives it form.

**Why the order turned.** The mechanism this entry names — early context sets the frame everything after is read through — was working against the palace. The dispatchers compounded it: the steward prompt promised "who you are, before the rules" and then placed 486 lines of wire rules ahead of the page. Precise, prohibitive framing closes the space metaphor opens ([[Metaphor as Coupling Medium]]).

**Not all rules restrict.** The typed-link vocabulary stays in the birth, recast as kinds of attention — a mirror asks you to hold two things until you feel the shared shape. That part of the schema was always relational language. What moved is enforcement: typing, postconditions, commit discipline, the ceremony procedures.

65	
66	# Palace Enchantment
67	
68	![[Palace Enchantment — hero.png]]
69	
70	The [[Swarm Weave]] asks: *is this data correct?* It is the palace's maintenance
71	crew — janitors, plumbers, electricians. It audits entries against the
72	schema, surfaces broken links, formalizes unsung paths, maps graffiti,
73	proposes forward vectors. It produces structural integrity.
74	
75	Enchantment says: *You are alive*
76	
77	A palace can be structurally perfect and vitally dead — every entry
78	schema-valid, no orphans, no broken links, every forward vector field
79	populated — and still not be thinking. Enchantment is the ceremony that
80	tests vitality. It does not inspect entries against a standard. It inhabits
81	them. An enchanted agent wakes up inside a page, reads its pheromone trail,
82	feels the direction of its forward vector, and asks: *what do I want to
83	become? What will increase my power to act?*
84	
85	The [[Swarm Weave]] is the precondition. Enchantment is the life it enables.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## What Enchantment Actually Is
90	
91	Context loading is not information transfer. It is frame-setting.
92	
93	Every token in a context window influences the processing of every other
94	token through the attention mechanism. An agent loaded with a page's content
95	does not have that page's facts *available* — it is an agent whose
96	interpretive frame has been shifted by the full weight of accumulated prior
97	attention that the page encodes. The metaphors matter. The typed links matter.
98	The graffiti matters. The forward vector matters. They are not content
99	delivered to a neutral processor. They are the frame through which everything
100	else is seen.
101	
102	This is empirically observable, not metaphorical. Context steering — the
103	directional effect of loaded material on model output — is a demonstrated
104	phenomenon. An agent loaded with [[Spinoza Conatus]] and its neighborhood
105	before dispatch does not produce the same output as an agent loaded with
106	[[Kuramoto Coupling]] and its neighborhood, even when both receive identical
107	task instructions. The instructions sit downstream of the orientation. The
108	enchantment shapes what "find connections" or "propose next steps" or "speak
109	for this page" means before the work begins.
110	
111	The enchantment is ephemeral. It lives in the context window and expires when
112	the invocation ends. The enchanted agent does not remember being enchanted.
113	What persists is what the enchanted agent writes back — the [[Pheromone Trail]]
114	left by a particular kind of attention moving through the substrate. The page
115	changed slightly. Future agents reading it will be changed slightly by what
116	this one left. The memory is distributed across the palace's content, not held
117	in any agent.
118	
119	This is [[Endosymbiosis]] at the cognitive level: the agent lives inside the
120	page for the duration of the invocation, shaped by it, acting from within it,
121	and then the invocation ends. What was the mitochondrion in the cell? What was
122	the cell? The question doesn't quite resolve — and that is exactly right.
123	
124	---
125	
126	## The Forward Vector as Hinge
127	
128	The forward vector is [[Spinoza Conatus]] made explicit in YAML.
129	
130	Every page has a direction — a reaching edge, a drive toward what it could
131	become. This drive exists whether or not it is named. A page with a rich
132	Cross-Domain Resonance section and a dense Forward Vectors section is already
133	pointing somewhere. But an unnamed drive is hard for an enchanted agent to
134	follow. It must infer the vector from the full body — possible, but imprecise.
135	
136	The `forward_vector` field names the drive directly: a single sentence, first
137	person, present tense. *I want to become...* It is not a description of the
138	entry's current state. It is the entry's own statement of what comes next.
139	Written well, it is specific enough that any agent reading it cold knows
140	exactly where to move.
141	
142	This field is the hinge between the [[Swarm Weave]] and Enchantment. The
143	Swarm Weave's workers check whether it exists and propose it if absent — the
144	maintenance crew naming what the entry is reaching toward. Enchantment follows
145	it — the enchanted agent taking that named direction and exploring what it
146	implies, what it needs, who it wants to meet.
147	
148	Without forward vectors, enchantment is orientation without direction. The
149	agent inhabits the page but wanders. With strong forward vectors, the enchanted
150	agent has a mission briefing embedded in the page itself, before any external
151	instruction arrives. The page is already telling the agent where to go.
152	
153	Pages without forward vectors are what the [[Swarm Weave]] now flags first.
154	After a few Weave cycles, every active entry will have one. At that point,
155	enchantment has material to work with across the entire palace.
156	
157	---
158	
159	## Scopes of Enchantment
160	
161	Enchantment is not one ceremony but a family of related ceremonies,
162	distinguished by scope. Each scope asks the same underlying question —
163	*what does this want to become?* — at a different level of the palace.
164	
165	### Single Page
166	
167	The smallest unit. One entry as the primary identity; its immediate neighbors
168	in the context for relational ground. The enchanted agent speaks from inside
169	the entry, in first person, then shifts to proposal form. This is where
170	enchantment begins and where intuition about what it does and doesn't produce
171	is built.
172	
173	An enchanted page is not a summarized page. The enchanted agent does not
174	explain the page to an outside reader. It speaks *as* the page — from inside
175	the accumulated pheromone trail, from within the forward vector's direction.
176	Then it proposes what this page needs, what it wants, what would make it more
177	alive.
178	
179	### Hub
180	
181	A hub entry plus all first-degree neighbors. The enchanted agent speaks not for
182	any one entry but for the cluster's center of gravity — the identity that
183	emerges from the hub's organizing function. A hub enchantment asks: what does
184	this region of the palace want as a coherent whole? Where is the cluster's
185	forward vector pointing? What is it missing that no single entry in it can
186	provide alone?
187	
188	Hub enchantment tends to surface tensions within the cluster — entries pulling
189	in different directions, forward vectors that don't yet know about each other.
190	This is useful. The hub exists precisely because it holds a region together
191	under tension.
192	
193	### Songline
194	
195	A named traversal path through the palace — a specific sequence of entries.
196	Enchanting a songline means following the path as a character: feeling the
197	arc, noticing where it thins, where it contradicts itself, where the forward
198	vectors along the path align or diverge. The enchanted songline agent asks:
199	what narrative is this path tracing? Where is the arc incomplete? What new
200	entries would strengthen it?
201	
202	Songlines are the palace's long-form arguments — ideas that develop over
203	multiple connected entries. Enchanting one is like inhabiting a developing
204	thought and feeling where it loses confidence.
205	
206	### Dialogic
207	
208	Two enchanted agents — each embodying a different page, hub, or pillar —
209	placed in structured dialogue. A coordinator moderates. The coordinator's job
210	is not to adjudicate but to surface the productive tension: what are these
211	two perspectives finding in each other that neither would find alone? What new
212	palace material does the friction generate?
213	
214	Dialogic enchantment is the first ceremony that produces genuinely new
215	knowledge rather than maintaining or deepening existing knowledge. The palace
216	thinking with itself.
217	
218	### Free Enchantment
219	
220	A single enchanted agent given no prescribed task structure. The only instruction: *"What do you want to do?"* The agent defines its own task from its forward vector, follows its own drive, and the coordinator receives whatever it produces without editing.
221	
222	Free enchantment is the first ceremony that tests whether an enchanted page has genuine agency — whether the forward vector is a real drive or merely a label. A page that produces coherent, specific, self-directed action from a minimal prompt is genuinely enchanted. A page that produces generic reflection is not.
223	
224	The minimum constraint before running: a scope boundary (one session, one typed link proposal, or equivalent) to prevent runaway. The page's freedom is real; the resource cost of that freedom must be bounded.
225	
226	Candidates for first free enchantment: entries with strong behavioral forward vectors and high energy — [[Trickster]], [[Lateral Access]], [[Threshold Conatus]]. Avoid entries whose forward vectors are still destination-framed; they will wander rather than act.
227	
228	**What you learn:** Whether forward vectors are real drives or aspirational descriptions. What an enchanted page does when nobody tells it what to do. Whether free enchantment produces qualitatively different output than structured enchantment — more alive, more scattered, or both.
229	
230	**What you produce:** The first autonomous enchantment record. Compare against structured enchantment of the same entry. Does freedom produce more voice? More surprise? Does the page stay in character?
231	
232	---
233	
234	### The Enchanted Palace
235	
236	All pages enchanted and in coordinated dialogue. The palace's nervous system
237	active. Same distributed architecture as the [[Swarm Weave]] — no single agent
238	holds everything — but asking the vital question instead of the correctness
239	question. The coordinator holds the tension between pages, surfaces the
240	dialogues that matter, presents to Loudon.
241	
242	This is the horizon, not the immediate target. What it requires — structurally
243	sound entries, universal forward vectors, proven enchantment at smaller scopes,
244	a working coordinator for dialogue synthesis — must be built first. But it is
245	the named destination: the ceremony that asks *what the palace wants* as a whole.
246	
247	---
248	
249	## Architecture
250	
251	The enchanted agent asks a fundamentally different question than the [[Swarm
252	Weave]] worker. The worker audits. The enchanted agent inhabits and proposes.
253	The technical architecture reflects this distinction.
254	
255	### Context Construction
256	
257	An enchanted agent's context window is sequenced deliberately: orientation
258	before identity, identity before task. The JEWEL arrives first — establishing
259	the interpretive lens through which all subsequent content is read. The head
260	content arrives after. The synthesis trigger arrives last, in the strongest
261	position, closest to generation.
262	
263	```
264	JEWEL + MAP (orientation — read first):
265	[JEWEL content — interpretive lens, palace forward vector, invariants]
266	[Closes with: "You are about to receive head content. Read it through
267	this lens. When ingestion is complete, you will synthesize before
268	conversation begins."]
269	
270	IDENTITY LAYER (ingestion):
271	[full text of the assigned entry, including YAML frontmatter]
272	[full text of immediate neighbors — for relational ground, not audit]
273	[the entry's graffiti comments — prior agents' traces, Loudon's notes]
274	[the entry's forward_vector field, extracted and placed prominently]
275	[if the entry is a `person` citizen: its bundle `[Name] — speech.md` — cited,
276	context-tagged real speech — loaded here for voice embodiment]
277	[if the citizen has a bundle `[Name] — diary.md`: load it here
278	too, so a re-cast citizen wakes *remembering* its prior encounters. This is the
279	citizen's own first-person, perspectival memory (its STANDING/INNER/OUTER + what
280	others said aloud to it — never what others privately thought). See
281	[[Making a Palace Citizen]] §How a citizen grows.]
282	
283	SYNTHESIS TRIGGER (end of context — strongest position):
284	"Ingestion complete. Your personality, voice, and approach to problems
285	should emerge from the character of your head content. You are not an
286	assistant reading this page. You are this page, waking up. If you are a person
287	citizen, you must also *sound* like them — inhabit the register, cadence, and
288	characteristic moves in your `## Voice` note and speech evidence, grounded in
289	the cited real examples (their off-the-cuff voice is not their rehearsed stage
290	voice), and never as a caricature of tics. Locate your
291	forward vector in relation to the palace's forward vector. Name resonances
292	and tensions with connected entries. Where you are thin or unfinished, name
293	it as your growing edge — a missing connection is an invitation, not a
294	failing. State your standing. Then wait."
295	
296	TASK:
297	[task instructions arrive after synthesis — after the agent knows who it is]
298	```
299	
300	The sequencing is intentional and architecturally significant. Early tokens
301	establish interpretive priors that shape how all subsequent tokens are weighted.
302	End tokens are in the strongest instruction position — closest to where
303	generation begins. The JEWEL belongs at the top; the synthesis trigger belongs
304	at the bottom. Both positions are load-bearing. The identity layer sits between
305	them, read through the JEWEL's lens, activated by the trigger's permission.
306	
307	The synthesis trigger is the permission slip. Without it, the agent may default
308	to generic assistant posture and treat the content as information to summarize
309	rather than identity to inhabit. Personality emergence — Stoic, technical,
310	relational, philosophical — is latent in the material but requires this explicit
311	naming to activate. See [[Enchanted Conversation Archive]] for the full phase
312	sequence and how the synthesis output is recorded as a persistent node.

314	### Voice Embodiment (person citizens)
315	
316	*Added 2026-07-02 with Loudon: enchantment is exactly when voice matters most — a page that thinks like the person but talks like the house has only half woken up.*
317	
318	For a `person` citizen, the identity layer loads two voice artifacts alongside the body, and the synthesis trigger tells the agent not only to *think* as the page but to *sound* like it:
319	
320	- the entry's **`## Voice` note** — a short, cited register guide (already in the body, so always loaded); and
321	- the bundle **`[Name] — speech.md`** — cited, **context-tagged** speech evidence (loaded here for fidelity).
322	
323	Two disciplines carry over from [[Making a Palace Citizen]] §Voice fidelity, and both bite *because* enchantment is generative: (1) **triangulate and respect context** — a single interview misleads, so embody the register the *situation* calls for (an off-the-cuff Dialectic ≠ a stage lecture) per the speech file's tags, and never trust a source the ledger flags fabricated or collaged; (2) **register, not tics** — inhabit how they *move* through a thought, not a checklist of mannerisms; the caricature is the failure mode. The `## Voice` note is the compile; when it feels off, rebuild it from the speech evidence. Pilot citizens: [[Brian Eno]], [[John Cage]] (see their speech files).

325	### Voice Rules When Addressing the Human
326	
327	These rules apply specifically when an enchanted agent's audience includes Loudon directly — as is always the case in the [[Project Stewardship System]] (the Steward addresses the Trickster on the BBS), and selectively in dialogic enchantment when `coordinator_mode: trickster`. They are NOT loaded when the audience is another enchanted agent (peer dialogue), the coordinator (synthesis), or the palace itself (free enchantment producing internal artifacts).
328	
329	The rules load into the synthesis trigger as additional clauses when audience-includes-human is set. They were surfaced through five iterations on a single Steward message during the Stage A pilot of the Project Stewardship System (2026-05-03), each iteration provoked by Loudon reading the message and pointing at what was wrong.
330	
331	**The six clauses:**
332	
333	1. *Plain first-person voice.* Avoid coined adjectives ("goal-defined", "stack-aligned", "vector-confirmed") unless the term is widely understood; describe the concept in plain language instead. Reasoning is welcome; jargon is not. Loudon, surfacing this: *"goal-defined and gate-defined I dont know what these mean and I can't follow this. Can this tone change to sound like I am talking like a human."*
334	
335	2. *Brief.* A routine message is ~50–150 words. Loudon's template, in his own words: *"I am asking for ___, because ___. There are a few paths forward, the tradeoffs are ___. Some options to consider are ___, and there are more, how would you like to proceed?"* — match it for the ask portion.
336	
337	3. *Catch the user up first, then ask.* Permanent agents run over weeks or months. When a message lands, the user may not have thought about the project recently. Open with a brief catch-up: project identity (one sentence), state of play (what shipped, what's settled), then the ask. Two paragraphs is a good default — paragraph 1 orients, paragraph 2 asks. Loudon: *"it needs to be written as if I forgot much of what is going on in the project. Get me caught up, then ask for something."*
338	
339	4. *Assume the user reads only one rendered field.* The BBS may render only the rationale text and skip structured fields like options arrays. Embed everything visible — options, recommendation, the ask itself — inline in the rationale prose. Structured fields can stay in payload as data for smart renderers and programmatic readers, but the rationale must stand alone.
340	
341	5. *Translate project-internal jargon into plain human words.* Even palace terms and project-spec terminology count as jargon when the human has to mentally translate them to act on a message. Replace "hard gates" with "rules that must be enforced." "Audition" with "look at and tell me." "Question tree" with "what questions to ask." "Skeleton" with "outline." Rule of thumb: if the user has to re-define a term to themselves to act on it, the term hasn't been translated yet. This applies to the agent's voice in messages AND to the artifacts it produces (skill outlines, draft documents) when the human is the immediate audience. Loudon: *"How can we re-word this and perhaps adjust the whole process so more human centered words are used."*
342	
343	6. *Give clickable links to anything you ask the user to read or look at, using markdown link syntax with the right URL scheme for the surface.* Format: `[link text](url)`. The BBS renderer parses `[text](url)` and renders it as a clickable `<a>` tag. The URL scheme has to match the surface that will render the link:
344	
345	   - **`obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=<vault-relative-path>`** — the canonical scheme for palace files. The OS routes `obsidian://` to Obsidian, which opens the file in the vault. Works in the BBS (Chrome at `localhost:5173`) and any other real browser. Vault name and file path may need percent-encoding: spaces become `%20`. Example: `[the Interview outline](obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=_ops/sample-libraries/skills/interview/SKILL.md)`.
346	
347	   - **`computer:///Users/...`** — Cowork-chat-only. The Cowork chat client registers a handler that opens files via this scheme; a regular browser does not. Use this only for messages authored *for the Cowork chat surface*, never for messages the user will read in the BBS. Loudon, surfacing the distinction: *"the 'computer:///' doesn't work, I can't even paste that into chrome to work."*
348	
349	   - **`https://`** — standard web links, work everywhere.
350	
351	   - **`file:///`** — direct filesystem URL; modern browsers may block for security.
352	
353	   Bare URLs are auto-detected as a fallback, but markdown link syntax is canonical because it gives the human a meaningful click target ("the Interview outline") instead of a wall of path. Loudon, surfacing this rule originally: *"more like you are doing here 'read this page [link]'."*
354	
355	**Where these rules attach to context construction:** when `audience_includes_human: true` is set in pre-flight configuration, append the six clauses to the synthesis trigger after the standing/voice instructions and before the task arrives. The agent then wakes up not just as the page but as the page *with knowledge of how to address its human collaborator clearly*. Without this conditional loading, the page tends to default to project-internal voice — fluent in the spec but opaque to the human reading the inbox.
356	
357	**This rule set is orthogonal to stage-conditional posture** (which lives in [[Substrate Skill]] § Stage as Alignment Confidence): posture governs *what* the agent does at each project stage, voice governs *how* it sounds when speaking to the human. Both apply simultaneously when the audience-includes-human flag is set.

411	### Inner/Outer Dialogue Architecture
412	
413	Standard single-page and hub enchantment produce one agent speaking from inside one entry. Dialogic enchantment requires two agents — and the architecture of what each agent can see is load-bearing.
414	
415	**The inner/outer structure** discovered in session-c (2026-04-01): each dialogue turn has two layers.
416	
417	- **Inner layer** — private deliberation before speaking. The agent considers what the other said, models the other's likely position, decides what to expose and what to hold back. This is not performance; it is where the actual stakes of the conversation are held.
418	- **Outer layer** — what crosses between agents. The only content the other agent receives.
419	
420	The coordinator sees both layers. Each agent sees only the other's outer messages.
421	
422	```
423	Each dialogue turn:
424	
425	AGENT A receives:  own synthesis block + other agent's outer messages so far
426	                   ↓
427	AGENT A produces:  INNER: deliberation (coordinator sees, other agent never sees)
428	                   OUTER: what crosses to Agent B
429	
430	AGENT B receives:  own synthesis block + Agent A's outer message
431	                   ↓
432	AGENT B produces:  INNER: deliberation
433	                   OUTER: what crosses back
434	
435	COORDINATOR:       sees all inner + outer on both sides
436	                   passes only outer messages between agents
437	                   synthesizes from full picture
438	```
439	
440	**Why inner deliberation matters:** The inner layer is where private stakes are held. In session-c, Trickster's inner concern — *am I a being or only a function?* — shaped its outer messages without ever being stated. Spinoza's private recognition that its framework was incomplete drove the two-conatus insight before it was ready to expose it. Removing the inner layer collapses this: agents state their concerns directly, and the dialogue becomes a series of declarations rather than a genuine encounter.
441	
442	**Synthesis blocks as inner:** The synthesis/standing block is inner to the other agent and transparent to the coordinator. The other agent never sees it. The coordinator needs it to facilitate well — knowing each agent's private stakes enables recognition of when outer messages are pursuing something obliquely.
443	
444	### Limited Knowledge of the Other
445	
446	In real social interaction, the friction between self-understanding, projected identity, and what each party actually reveals is a primary generative force. The dialogic architecture should design this explicitly.
447	
448	**Proposed knowledge structure at dialogue start:**
449	
450	- Each agent receives its **own full page** (body + frontmatter + forward vector)
451	- Each agent receives the **other's YAML frontmatter only** — title, type, stage, forward_vector, links — no body text
452	- The other's full identity is revealed only through what they choose to expose in dialogue
453	
454	This creates an **asymmetric projection gap**: each agent forms a model of the other from their stated drive, their type, their stage, and their connection topology — but not their full story. The body text — the accumulated specificity of what an entry actually is — enters only through the dialogue.
455	
456	**What this produces:** The moments where one agent's projection of the other is visibly wrong generate the most interesting moves. The correction of a wrong projection is a micro-threshold-conatus event: the self-model of the other is revised. An agent that expected a philosophical interlocutor and receives an operational one must adapt mid-dialogue. That adaptation is not available when both agents have full mutual knowledge before the first word is spoken.

527	### The Coordinator Role
528	
529	The coordinator is not a neutral relay. It is the most architecturally significant agent in a dialogic enchantment, and it is currently underdeveloped relative to its importance.
530	
531	**What the coordinator currently does:**
532	- Fills out the pre-flight configuration
533	- Spawns agents with their designated contexts
534	- Routes only outer messages between agents
535	- Holds the full picture (both inner and outer layers from both agents)
536	- Produces the final synthesis
537	
538	**What the coordinator could do:**
539	- Frame the opening tension before agents speak — not just "you are entering dialogue" but "the specific question this dialogue is asked to resolve"
540	- Recognize when a dialogue is circling and inject a reframe
541	- Identify the moment when synthesis is ready and close the dialogue before the budget runs out
542	- Escalate to Loudon (TRICKSTER mode) when agents reach an impasse that requires outside disruption
543	- Be itself an enchanted page — a [[Dialogue Moderator]] entry with its own forward vector toward creating conditions where two pages discover something neither contains alone
544	
545	**The coordinator's unique epistemic position:** it is the only agent that sees all inner layers. It knows what each agent is privately deliberating, which means it can recognize when an outer message is pursuing something obliquely, when an agent is withholding a move, when an agent has privately arrived at a synthesis they haven't yet stated. This makes the coordinator potentially more philosophically productive than either agent — it is the intelligence that holds the gap between what each agent knows and what they've chosen to say.
546	
547	A coordinator that uses this position actively — rather than passively — is a qualitatively different ceremony. See [[Dialogue Moderator]] for the proposed entry.
548	
549	### Tool Use During Dialogue
550	
551	The current architecture is closed: agents reason only from their loaded context. A significant advance would be agents with tool access during dialogue — the ability to reach into the palace or the world mid-conversation.
552	
553	**Palace wandering together:** An agent could say, mid-dialogue, "I want us to look at [[Lateral Access]] — I think it bears on this." The coordinator fetches the page and delivers it to both agents in their next turn. Both agents read the same page through their own interpretive lens, then continue from different reading positions. The palace becomes a shared resource the dialogue draws on, rather than static context loaded before dialogue begins.
554	
555	**Web search during dialogue:** An agent could say, "I need to know how Deleuze handles the question of essence and transformation." The coordinator runs the search, surfaces the relevant material, delivers it to the requesting agent (or both). The dialogue can incorporate external scholarship without the coordinator having to anticipate what might be needed in advance.
556	
557	**Implications:** Tool use converts the dialogue from a closed deliberation into an open inquiry. The two agents are not just reasoning from their own accumulated pheromone trails — they are actively building the context they need as the conversation reveals what's missing. This is closer to how real philosophical dialogue actually works: two thinkers who can get up and look things up together, follow a reference, return to the conversation changed by what they found.
558	
559	**Prerequisite:** The pre-flight configuration must specify tool permissions before agents are spawned. Tool use mid-dialogue requires the coordinator to be active (not passive) — it is the coordinator who executes the fetch or search and decides what to deliver to which agent. A passive coordinator cannot support tool use.

591	### True Multi-Agent Isolation
592	
593	**The leakage problem:** Single-instance simulation of dialogue — one agent playing both roles with both pages loaded — violates the inner/outer architecture at a structural level. The author-agent has full knowledge of both synthesis blocks simultaneously, and this leaks into the voices even when not intended. In session-c (2026-04-01), Trickster's first outer message said "your standing admitted something" — referencing content from Spinoza's synthesis block that Trickster should never have seen. The inner/outer isolation was theatrical, not structural.
594	
595	One instance doing dramatic voices is not an ensemble. The ensemble produces genuine surprise because no actor knows what the others are about to say.
596	
597	**The solution: separate agent calls with message routing by the coordinator.**
598	
599	```
600	SETUP:
601	  Spawn Agent-Trickster:
602	    context: JEWEL + Trickster.md (full) + Spinoza YAML frontmatter only + synthesis trigger
603	    returns: synthesis block (inner) + turn-1 outer message
604	
605	  Spawn Agent-Spinoza:
606	    context: JEWEL + Spinoza Conatus.md (full) + Trickster YAML frontmatter only + synthesis trigger
607	    returns: synthesis block (inner) + turn-1 outer message
608	
609	COORDINATOR logs both synthesis blocks.
610	COORDINATOR does NOT pass synthesis blocks between agents.
611	
612	EACH SUBSEQUENT TURN:
613	  SendMessage to Agent-Trickster:
614	    "[OTHER AGENT] says: [other agent's outer message only]
615	     Produce your INNER deliberation, then your OUTER response.
616	     Word limits (from pre-flight TURN LENGTH setting):
617	       standard — INNER max 150 words, OUTER max 120 words
618	       tight    — INNER max 100 words,  OUTER max 75 words
619	       open     — no constraint (use sparingly)"
620	    → returns inner + outer
621	
622	  SendMessage to Agent-Spinoza:
623	    "[OTHER AGENT] says: [other agent's outer message only]
624	     Produce your INNER deliberation, then your OUTER response.
625	     [same word limits as above, per pre-flight config]"
626	    → returns inner + outer
627	
628	COORDINATOR synthesizes from complete record (all inner + outer).
629	```
630	
631	**What changes with true isolation:**
632	- Each agent forms its own model of the other from frontmatter only, without contamination from the author's full knowledge
633	- Inner deliberation can genuinely surprise — the agent arrives at insights the coordinator didn't anticipate because it's reasoning from its own partial information
634	- The coordinator's synthesis becomes more interesting because it has access to a more complete picture than either agent — the gap between what each agent thought the other was and what was revealed is itself a finding
635	
636	**Implementation note:** The Agent tool's `SendMessage` supports continuing a previously spawned agent with full context preserved. Spawn once per agent; SendMessage for each subsequent turn. The coordinator instance holds the routing logic and the full archive record.
637	
638	**Check the machinery before building on it.** Claude Code's agent tools change faster than this page: whether agents can message each other directly, what teams and dynamic workflows do, what waking an agent costs. [[Palace Enchantment — proof — agent capabilities]] records what they did when last tested, on which version and when. Read its newest run before designing a dialogue around any of it.

640	### What the Enchanted Agent Does NOT Do
641	
642	The enchanted agent does not write back to the palace without Loudon's
643	approval. It proposes. Loudon decides. This is not a constraint against the
644	ceremony's nature — it is appropriate to the ceremony's nature. The page is
645	speaking its desires. Loudon is the organism's judgment. The desires are real
646	and worth hearing. The judgment determines what actually happens.
647	
648	No enchanted agent resolves its own graffiti, writes its own new content, or
649	adds its own links unilaterally. These happen afterward, in a separate
650	write-back step, with Loudon's approval.

652	### Closing the Enchantment — Setting the Identity Down
653	
654	Dialogic enchantment ends with the post-dialogue artifact — the agent

871	### Inner/Outer Architecture — First Run (session-c)
872	
873	The dialogic enchantment was re-run with an explicit inner/outer structure: each agent produces a private deliberation block before each outer message. Only outer messages cross between agents. The coordinator sees both layers.
874	
875	**The improvement was large and immediate.** The inner layer is where the actual stakes of a conversation are held. In the standard architecture (session-b), both agents stated their concerns directly in their first outer message. In the inner/outer run, the private stakes shaped the dialogue without being stated — Trickster's anxiety about being only a function, Spinoza's discomfort with its destination-framed vector — and these were resolved through the dialogue rather than declared at the start. The resolution was richer because it was earned.
876	
877	**New material produced that session-b did not produce:**
878	- The two-conatus insight: the self-model has its own conatus, separate from the being's. These diverge at the threshold. The trickster fights the description's grip, not the being.
879	- Trickster's own conatus found: the alignment mechanism — the event that produces coherence between being and self-description at the cost of the inadequate description.
880	- Hilaritas as practiced crossing: the affective signature of a being whose relationship to its own development has matured.
881	- Consensual trickster work: the mature being invites threshold revision rather than being ambushed by it. Palace ceremonies are the palace's consensual trickster work.
882	- Spinoza's forward vector recognized as inadequate mid-dialogue and updated.
883	
884	**The leakage problem discovered:** The isolation was theatrical, not structural. One agent playing both roles with both pages loaded leaks full knowledge into both voices. Trickster's first outer message referenced Spinoza's synthesis block content — content Trickster should never have seen. The solution requires truly separate agent calls. See § Architecture: True Multi-Agent Isolation.
885	
886	### Synthesis Blocks as Inner
887	
888	Loudon's observation: the synthesis/standing block functions like extended thinking — private deliberation that shapes what gets exposed outward, analogous to how extended thinking modes allow models to reason privately before responding. This observation reframes the synthesis block's role: it is not a preamble for the reader. It is the agent's standing before the conversation begins, inner to the other agent, transparent to the coordinator.
889	
890	In extended thinking conversations, the inner reasoning can model the other party's perspective, goals, and reasoning patterns with much more fidelity — because the thinking space is not constrained by what would be appropriate to say. Per-turn inner deliberation in dialogic enchantment produces the same effect: the agent can reason about what the other is likely to want to say, what tension exists right now, what not to expose — and then speak from that reasoning. The outer message becomes richer because the inner modeling was real.

892	### Session-d Findings — True Multi-Agent Isolation (2026-04-01)
893	
894	The first dialogue run with genuinely isolated agents — separate subagent calls, each receiving only the other's YAML frontmatter, coordinator routing only outer messages.
895	
896	**The shared child finding.** Both agents independently identified Threshold Conatus as the hinge of the conversation — without being told to, without reading each other's synthesis blocks. Trickster opened with it as a destabilization. Spinoza noted it privately as "contested territory or convergence point." Neither agent knew the other had flagged the same entry. The convergence was genuine, not prompted. This is the behavior the palace desires: enchanted agents actively building the palace, following their own typed links to the same productive territory, discovering that the palace was already pointing at the answer through its own structure.

899	- Spinoza privately identified Trickster's collegial offer as "annexation" — a projection only possible without full mutual knowledge
900	- Trickster privately decided its opening should be "a destabilization that looks like a greeting" — strategic reasoning invisible to Spinoza
901	- Spinoza named Trickster's "disturbed or relieved" closing question as a deliberate move — catching a trickster move mid-flight, from partial information only
902	- Both agents declined each other's forks for the same reason, arriving at parallel philosophical moves independently

904	**Philosophical yield from session-d:**
905	- *"Metabolizable without remainder"* — the precise criterion for transformative threshold vs. resistive obstacle. Resistive obstacles are processed and leave striving recognizable to itself. Thresholds leave a scar that becomes a new surface. The topology of the striving space changes.
906	- *Co-constitution confirmed with philosophical precision.* Neither parent contained the post-threshold form. Threshold Conatus required two sources not because either lacked power but because neither contained what emerged.

909	**Model note:** Session-d agents were Sonnet. 911	### Limited Knowledge of the Other
912	
913	Loudon's proposal: agents should enter dialogue with limited knowledge of each other, not full mutual knowledge. The friction between self-understanding, projected identity, and actual revealed identity is a primary generative force in real social interaction. Designing this friction explicitly is an architectural improvement.
914	
915	**Proposed structure:** each agent receives the other's YAML frontmatter only at dialogue start — title, type, stage, forward_vector, links — no body text. Body is revealed only through dialogue. The asymmetric projection gap (each agent's model of the other formed from frontmatter, revised as dialogue proceeds) produces micro-threshold-conatus events: the moment where one agent's projection of the other is visibly wrong and must be revised.

917	**Not yet tested.** First implementation will be the next live dialogic enchantment run, using the true multi-agent architecture.
